recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Further edits would either duplicate existing guidance or touch generated-looking diagram/tool-tip fragments rather than change implementer understanding.
issue_request: FHIR-20688 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I clarification for R5 asking whether Resource.meta.source identifies a source system, a full source resource URI, or something broader; the approved resolution was to allow a fully qualified resource reference, an abstract identifier, or a service endpoint while avoiding an exclusive Provenance.entity.what[x] mapping.
initial_application: Git commit 9edd51287b10ae90910262893cc060ad9df66f0b directly applied FHIR-20688 by updating source/datatypes/meta.xml and source/resource/resource-notes.xml so Meta.source could be more general or abstract and the Resource metadata table no longer pointed only to Provenance.entity.what[x].
additional_context: Related Published issue FHIR-20906 clarified that Meta.source may correspond to Provenance.agent.who as well as Provenance.entity.what and is already represented on the combined branch by a source-changing reconciliation commit. Later Applied issue FHIR-49878 clarified the definition as a data source rather than only a source system, and FHIR-15659 updated stale Provenance choice names from what[x]/who[x] to what/who.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. On the latest combined branch, source/datatypes/meta.xml identifies Meta.source as a data source, allows non-FHIR/server and structure-fragment examples, and says it may correspond to Provenance.entity.what or Provenance.agent.who while remaining more general or abstract; source/resource/resource-notes.xml also describes broad source granularity.
